definition: A change in position, given as a vector: from A to B it is $\overrightarrow{AB} = \boldsymbol{b} - \boldsymbol{a}$, which depends only on the start and end points and not on the route, so it is not the distance travelled; in one dimension it is a signed distance, such as a position measured from the origin.

The position of B relative to A is the vector from A to B, $\overrightarrow{AB} = \boldsymbol{b} - \boldsymbol{a}$ (B's position minus A's, not the other way round); for two moving objects it is $\boldsymbol{r}_{B}(t) - \boldsymbol{r}_{A}(t)$ at the same time $t$, and its magnitude is the distance between them.
